title: Anomaly blitz runbook: microburst throughput & latency triage
body:
Summary:
Quick (45m) cross-team blitz to capture a recurring microburst pattern seen on 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29 on canary and a small % of prod clusters. Symptoms: short ~30s spikes of 2x p95 and sustained 20–30% throughput drop for ~60–90s. No full node OOMs, no obvious GPU driver crashes.

Attendees:
- Priya Nandakumar (owner)
- Ethan Morales (observability)
- Samira Patel (serving runtime)
- Leo Chen (kernel/compilation)
- Maya Ortiz (SRE)
- Ravi Gupta (benchmarks)

What we observed (rapid notes):
- Spike windows correlate with sudden drop in QPS served (from baseline 1200 qps -> ~800 qps) for affected shards.
- p50 relatively stable, p95 and p99 move. Example from grafana snapshot: p50 12ms -> 14ms, p95 85ms -> 180ms, p99 240ms -> 420ms.
- GPU utilization dips slightly during spike (~72% -> ~60%) while CPU on host climbs ~8–12%.
- KV cache hit rate decreased by ~6 percentage points coincident with spikes on some shards.
- Warmup traces show increased cold-start-like behavior for long-sequence requests (seq_len > 1024).
- No matching kernel rollout events in cluster metadata; compilation metrics around time show slight increase in kernel-switch counts on a subset of hosts.

Quick hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache eviction storm: noisy tenants evict prefixes -> increased recompute for long sequences -> higher tail latency.
2) NUMA/CPU contention causing jitter in CPU-side scheduling of input processing leading to reduced batching efficiency.
3) Kernel selector flip on some shards: runtime chooses different matmul kernel under certain seq_len distribution -> throughput drop.
4) Brief network saturation to parameter server (for hybrid cache layout) causing backend stalls.

Data to gather (immediate):
- Ethan: collect aligned traces for 09-28/09-29 windows (span IDs, timeline) and export 1s-resolution KV hit/miss with shard mapping. (ETA EOD)
- Maya: collect host-level metrics (irq, softirq, ctx switches, iowait) for affected host list and correlate with pod allocations. (ETA +8h)
- Samira: run reproducer on canary with synthetic microburst generator (script below) and toggles: KV cache disabled, smaller kv cache TTL, force kernel-selection=legacy. Capture batch sizes and warmup counters. (ETA +24h)
- Leo: check kernel-switch logs and compile-variant counts for PR #4123 timeframe; instrument a small metric in kernel-selector to count variant flips. (ETA +48h)
- Ravi: run 6 x 30s stress runs (production traffic replay) and gather p50/p95/p99 + gpu_util per run. Attach diffs versus baseline. (ETA +24h)

Reproducer (quick):
- Purpose: simulate noisy prefixes + a burst of long seq requests and observe batching + kv behavior.
- Steps:
  1) Start canary endpoint with config: max_batch_size=64, batching_window_ms=8, kv_cache_enabled=true, kv_cache_capacity=500k entries.
  2) Warmup: send 60s of baseline small-chats (seq_len 64–128) at 1200 qps.
  3) Burst: for 30s, send 30% of traffic as long-seq requests (seq_len 1536) at same total qps; at the same time inject 10% of traffic with synthetic high-entropy prefixes to force kv churn.
  4) Observe: collect per-request latency, batch size distribution, kv hit/miss, and kernel-selection counts.
- Script snippet (dev-run):
  python tools/microburst_sim.py --target canary://redwood-canary-3 --duration 90 --burst-seq-len 1536 --burst-share 0.3 --noisy-prefix-share 0.1 --qps 1200

Preliminary quick-run notes (Samira did an initial run during the meeting):
- With KV cache disabled, p95 drop during burst is ~40% less severe. Indicates KV churn plays big role.
- Forcing kernel-selection=legacy (older matmul path) removed the immediate throughput drop on 2/6 hosts in the run; suggests selector flip matters.
- Batch size distribution during spike skews to smaller batches (mean batch size 12 -> 7).

Immediate mitigations proposed (canary-only to start):
- Short-term: apply small kv_cache_ttl increase (+30s) for canary clusters to reduce eviction storms; enable sticky-prefix guard to reduce noisy-prefix influence. (Owner: Priya; ETA 2h)
- Medium-term: add metric for kernel-selector flips and alert when flips > 5/min per host; deploy to canary. (Owner: Leo; ETA 48h)
- SRE: throttle noisy tenants if detected via prefix-entropy heuristic (pilot rule). (Owner: Maya; ETA 24h)

Action items (with owners & checkpoints):
- Priya: deploy kv_cache_ttl bump to canary + monitor 6h window; report delta in next sync. (checkpoint: 6h)
- Ethan: upload full trace bundle to GCS and tag JIRA-8892; provide per-span correlation table. (checkpoint: uploaded)
- Samira & Ravi: run reproducibility matrix across 3 canary hosts with and without cache + legacy kernel path; summary doc to /serving-runtime/benchmarks/ (checkpoint: doc link)
- Leo: instrument kernel-selector flip metric; open small PR for runtime (target: hotfix branch). (checkpoint: PR created)
- Maya: propose temporary k8s QoS tweak (cpuManagerPolicy/steal prevention) and run on staging. (checkpoint: staging test)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is noisy-prefix detection mature enough to use as an automated throttle without impacting real customers? (Samira + Product)
- Do we need to change default kernel selection thresholds for sequence lengths near the observed edge-case? (Leo + Compilers)
- Can we tighten the observability window granularity for kv-cache metrics to sub-second resolution without heavy overhead? (Ethan + Observability infra)

Notes to self: informal observations and TODOs
- We should capture <1s batch-size distribution histograms during bursts (current 1s rollups hide spikes).
- Add a synthetic "prefix-entropy" label to the request context so we can correlate in traces without storing raw text (privacy).
- Consider running a controlled experiment with isolated noisy-tenant pods to measure eviction thresholds.

Meeting artifacts & links:
- Reproducer script: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tools/microburst_sim.py
- PR for kernel selector instrumentation: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123
- Jira: JIRA-8892 (microburst investigation)
- Grafana snapshot: grafana/dashboard/snapshot/abc123

Next sync: Fri 2026-10-02 09:30 PT (15 min) to review canary results and decide on wider rollout of kv_ttl tweak.

End notes: keep this doc as living runbook; prefer short iterative changes and canary-only rollouts until we have strong repro and root cause.

---
Version log (short):
- 2026-09-30: initial blitz notes captured during meeting.
- 2026-10-01: added action owners and reproducer results from quick-run.
